description: Gate B16_LEDGER: relative tolerance of the identity countries + bunker account = objective (incl. the fixed-once constants)

Decision 91a ledger rules (both scenarios): (1) every objective term is a direct cost of the owner of its component - new capacity (p_nom_opt - p_nom) x capital_cost, marginal cost x flow x weight, fixed-once constants (existing asset FOM, existing cross-border FOM) - as in gate A5; own facilities, fuels and extra-ASEAN imports -> own country; domestic gas at the decision-43 price is the producing country's generator cost; one-port components belong to the country of their country column (e.g. national ammonia demand on the regional ammonia bus) else to the entity of their bus; (2) cross-border lines / links (incl. existing) -> the corridor, its costs and its congestion rent (settlement surplus) split half / half between the two countries (main) or by in-country length (sensitivity, XB_LENGTH_SHARES_S4D3.csv); (3) every component port on a bus of another entity is settled at that bus's dual (marginal_price x weight): cross-border electricity / H2 / gas / CO2 exchanges at each end's nodal dual, liquid-fuel purchases and sales of a country at the regional bus dual, bunker fuel at the regional dual into the separate 'ASEAN bunker account' subject (no country), CO2 shipping freight -> exporter and the storage service at the receiver's 'co2 sequestered <j>' dual (exporter pays, receiver is paid), Lao transit freight -> LA; (4) the regional liquid pool has no owner: its surplus (rents of binding limits on regional supply; zero by LP duality when none binds) is the difference term; (5) gate B16_LEDGER: |countries + bunker account - objective (incl. constants)| <= 1e-6 x |objective|, in both acceptance sets

NODAL_PRICES.csv (wide, one row per bus = node x carrier): the dual price (buses_t.marginal_price, EUR per MWh or t) aggregated to calendar days as the snapshot-weighted mean (one column per day), plus the weighted mean, min and max over the run
